Definition: hither or thither (but used both of place and time)
BiblicalUsage: Hennah means hither, to this place, and it is the word of summons and of return. In Genesis 15:16 God tells Abram the fourth generation shall come hither again, in Joshua 3:9 Joshua says come hither and hear the words of the Lord, and in Genesis 42:15 Joseph says hereby ye shall be proved.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word is a call to come closer: the generation comes back, the people come to hear, and the brothers are proved by what they do when they come hither.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
